title: Margins
description: A printed lyric sheet you mark up with a pencil. Scribble a loop, a line or an arrow and it is read and redrawn as a confident graphite mark: a circle around a word, an underline, a strike-through, a bracket on a verse, or an arrow out to the margin where a handwritten note appears; Rub out takes the last mark back.
intent: Annotation as a gesture you can be sloppy with: the sheet understands what you meant and draws it the way a sure hand would, in pencil with graphite tooth, so marking up a lyric feels like reading it closely.
sources: herb reference board: 387b selection callout and 7463 hand lettering
